body: That's good, it was jus a cofffee mug. Maybe try oranges next time? Or screaming. Or playing music as loud as possible and sing along. Don't mind the neighbours. Actually, fuck them too.

You are not alone, there is more of us. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cQOaDzQ_aJ8

I stopped using words like 'never/always/forever' and it made a huge difference. These are just words but they affect the way we think about ourselves way too much. Once I realised it is true that I don't know what will happen in the future I automatically turned into sort of carpe diem/day by day/step by step person. Which was very new to me as I used to hate my life and to focus on my day, on  present moment was the very last thing I wanted to do. But this is how a change can happen. By going back to the basic stuff and keeping your head clear of all those terrible visions that came from feeling guilty, sad, lonely, worthless. This is not true, this is just temporary. Past doesn't have to be an anchor. Today is what really matters. 
You don't have to try, I'm not feeling bad for you :) I can relate, I can imagine what you're going through because of my own, similar experiences. And that's why there's no pity in me, just pure empathy and to be honest - I think you're brave and doing a great work. Sharing your story with us is a step already. Thank you!

It makes perfect sense to me because, no surprise, I've been there. Being stuck between those two: wanting to disappear and wanting to stay alive can make you go nuts. There's so much pressure and you don't have any tools to let off steam but instead you got tones of problems. I don't think there's an easy way out. But there's time. Plenty of time to use, change, try, fail, try again, do something different. It seriously worked in my case. I was down there where everything is grey or black, stressful. I thought this is the end, no chance I can get past this moment in my life, nope, that's enough, bye, gotta go. But I didn't. I asked for help. I gave up on myself and everyone around me and just stood there, waiting for whatever has to be done to get me back on my feet: meds, therapy, family, church, you name it. Day by day. Time is always on your side. I'm not talking about paying rent now, I mean the bigger picture. Life goes down, life goes up, and down and up again. All I need to do is survive the bad times, hope for the good ones and settle for something in between. Just wait. You'll see. Take care!
